theme.title: Quiet Session
theme.summary: Real Estate (+0.17%) and Financials (+0.10%) led the market today, while Health Care (-0.22%) and Industrials (-0.10%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged -0.03%, defensives -0.06%, and value/cyclicals +0.05% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 +0.65%, Dow +0.13%, Nasdaq +0.81% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at +0.24%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 0.75% to 14.52, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 1.15% to $4,429.90, crude oil was little changed at $81.33, and bitcoin slipped 1.12% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
